newsitem.title: CANADA: Transocean wins Canada drilling contract.
newsitem.headline: Transocean wins Canada drilling contract.

text.p: Partners in Canada's Terra Nova oil project said on Wednesday they awarded Houston-based Transocean Offshore Inc a contract to supply the semi-submersible rig for drilling and completing wells for the project.

The drilling unit, Transocean Explorer, currently operating in the North Sea, was contracted for a two years with three one-year options. The Transocean Explorer is scheduled to start drilling in the spring of 1998, the Terra Nova Alliance said.

Terra Nova is the second major offshore oil project off Canada's east coast. Located 350 km (217 miles) southeast of the province of Newfoundland, the field harbors and estimated 400 million barrels of oil.
Drilling activity is still subject to regulatory approval and a decision by its owners to go ahead, both expected this autumn.

The alliance said the Transocean Explorer would be upgraded before drilling on Canada's Grand Banks. Modifications were expected to take about three months and cost between C$58 million and C$74 million.
Eastern Canadian shipyards were to be invited to tender for the work.
The alliance said that up to 44 wells may be required to develop the Terra Nova field. Plans called for wells to be drilled in clusters of about six.

Partners in the development include operator Petro-Canada with 34.2 percent, Mobil Corp unit Mobil Oil Canada with 20.7 percent, Husky Oil Ltd with 15.8 percent, Norsk Hydro A/S with 15 percent, Murphy Oil Corp with 10.7 percent and Mosbacher Operating Co with 3.6 percent. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
